newsitem.title: UK: Tarmac pledges to cut gearing over 2-3 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Tarmac pledges to cut gearing over 2-3 yrs.

text.p: Tarmac Plc, the British builder which reported a 58.3 million stg pretax loss on Tuesday due to a 65 million charge, pledged to address concerns about high debt levels, saying it would cut gearing back over the coming years.
Finance director Chris Bunker told a news conference: "Debt is at an unacceptable level and the management is focused on reducing our borrowings."
He said he aimed to cut the 66 percent gearing level back to 30 to 40 percent over the next two to three years.
Group debt rose in the six months to June 30 to 511.6 million stg, up 163.5 million.
Tarmac said it would reduce this debt level through a range of efforts.
"We will improve profit margins and the quality of earnings," said the finance chief.
He also pledged to make further cost reductions which go beyond the savings gleaned from the integration of the Wimpey businesses acquired in an asset swap earlier his year.
Savings from integration are seen at more than 35 million stg a year. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
